description: Question sets for Community Builder v2. Band 1 is visual matching (no text questions). Bands 2-3 use text questions with grade-tiered progression matching the maths-dive system. Each question set has a grade_id for the progression engine.

progression_rules.note: Band 1 uses visual matching (tap building/vehicle). Bands 2-3 use text questions. Grade mastery = 85% of last 10. Band mastery = 19/20 at top grade. Cross-band warmup loads previous band's top grade.

band_1_matching.note: Band 1 visual matching config. All buildings pre-placed. Player taps matching building + vehicle.

questions.question: Who drives the bus that takes you to school?
questions.hint: They sit at the front of the big yellow bus.

questions.question: What colour is a school bus?
questions.hint: It's a bright, sunny colour so cars can see it easily.

questions.question: What should you do when you get on a bus?
options: Sit down and wear your seatbelt
questions.hint: Sitting safely keeps you from getting hurt if the bus stops suddenly.

questions.question: Where does a bus stop to pick people up?
options: In the middle of the road
questions.hint: Look for a sign with a picture of a bus.

questions.question: Why is public transit important for a community?
options: It helps people who don't have cars get around
questions.hint: Buses and trains are for everyone in the community.

questions.question: What does a taxi do?
options: Takes people where they need to go for a fare
questions.hint: You can call one when you need a ride.

questions.question: Why is it important to share the road?
options: Cars, buses, bikes, and pedestrians all need space to travel safely
Because the road is too big for one car
questions.hint: Everyone has a right to travel safely.

questions.question: What is a 'route' on a bus map?
options: The path the bus follows with its stops
The time the bus was built
questions.hint: Each bus follows a set path through the community.

questions.question: Who cooks food at a restaurant?
questions.hint: They wear a tall white hat in the kitchen!

questions.question: Where does a chef prepare meals?
questions.hint: A room with ovens, pots, and pans.

questions.question: What is one food group that keeps you healthy?
questions.hint: Apples, carrots, and bananas are all part of this group.

questions.question: Why do communities need restaurants?
options: So people can buy prepared food
So cars have a place to park
questions.hint: Sometimes families want someone else to cook a meal.

questions.question: Where does the food in our community come from before it reaches the restaurant?
questions.hint: Farmers grow the ingredients that chefs use.

questions.question: Why is it important for restaurants to follow food safety rules?
options: To keep people from getting sick
questions.hint: Clean kitchens and proper cooking stop germs.

questions.question: What is a tradition many Canadian families share around food?
questions.hint: In October, many families share a big meal together.

questions.question: How do different cultures in our community share their heritage through food?
options: By opening restaurants with food from their home countries
questions.hint: You might find Italian, Chinese, Indian, and many other foods in your community.

questions.question: Who builds houses and roads?
questions.hint: They wear a hard hat and use big machines.

questions.question: What does a stop sign tell you to do?
questions.hint: It is red and has eight sides.

questions.question: Why do construction workers wear hard hats?
questions.hint: Things might fall at a building site.

questions.question: What do street lights help us do at night?
options: See the road and stay safe
questions.hint: They shine bright light on streets and sidewalks.

questions.question: Why do communities need roads and sidewalks?
options: So people and vehicles can travel safely
questions.hint: Roads connect homes, schools, and shops.

questions.question: What does a warning sign with an orange diamond shape mean?
questions.hint: Orange signs warn about work zones.

questions.question: Why is a fire hydrant important for a community?
options: Firefighters connect hoses to it for water
questions.hint: These colourful objects on sidewalks are connected to water pipes underground.

questions.question: What is 'infrastructure'?
options: The basic things a community needs, like roads and pipes
questions.hint: Roads, bridges, water pipes, and electrical wires are all part of this.

questions.question: Who helps you feel better when you are sick?
questions.hint: They wear a white coat and use a stethoscope.

questions.question: Where does a doctor work?
questions.hint: A big building with a red cross on it.

questions.question: What tool does a doctor use to listen to your heart?
questions.hint: It has two earpieces and a round end.

questions.question: What vehicle rushes sick people to the hospital?
questions.hint: It has flashing lights and a loud siren.

questions.question: Why do communities need hospitals?
options: So sick or hurt people can get help nearby
questions.hint: When there's an emergency, people need help close to home.

questions.question: What is one way to stay healthy in your community?
questions.hint: Clean hands help stop germs from spreading.

questions.question: Who else works at a hospital besides doctors?
questions.hint: A whole team of health workers cares for patients.

questions.question: Why is it important to visit the doctor even when you are not sick?
questions.hint: Check-ups help catch problems before they get big.

questions.question: Who grows the food we eat?
questions.hint: They work on land with crops and animals.

questions.question: Which of these grows on a farm?
questions.hint: It is tall, green, and you can eat it!

questions.question: Where does milk come from?
questions.hint: Moo! This animal gives us milk.

questions.question: What does a farmer sell at a market?
questions.hint: Fresh, yummy things they grew themselves.

questions.question: Why are farms important to a community?
options: They provide food for people to eat
questions.hint: Without farms, stores would have no food to sell.

questions.question: What is a farmers' market?
options: A place where farmers sell food directly to people
A store that sells farm tools
questions.hint: You can buy fresh apples, vegetables, and eggs there.

questions.question: How do the seasons affect what a farmer can grow?
options: Different crops grow in different seasons
questions.hint: Strawberries ripen in summer but not in January.

questions.question: How does food get from the farm to the grocery store?
options: Trucks, trains, or ships carry it
questions.hint: Big vehicles move large amounts of food across the province.

questions.question: Who puts out fires in our community?
questions.hint: They wear a red helmet and drive a big red truck!

questions.question: What does a fire truck carry?
questions.hint: Fires need lots of water to go out.

questions.question: If there is a fire, what number do you call?
questions.hint: This special number gets help fast.

questions.question: Where do firefighters work?
questions.hint: The big red building with the fire trucks inside.

questions.question: Why should every home have a smoke alarm?
options: To warn people about fires early
questions.hint: Smoke alarms make a loud sound when they sense smoke.

questions.question: What should your family practise at home for fire safety?
questions.hint: Everyone should know how to get out safely.

questions.question: Firefighters also help with which other emergencies?
questions.hint: They help people who are trapped or hurt.

questions.question: What is the firefighter's rule about matches and lighters?
questions.hint: These things can start fires and are not for kids.

questions.question: Who helps you find books to read?
questions.hint: They work in a building full of books.

questions.question: What is a library for?
questions.hint: You can take a book home and bring it back when you're done!

questions.question: What is one rule at the library?
options: Shout as loud as you can
questions.hint: People need quiet to read and think.

questions.question: What else can you do at a library besides read books?
options: Use a computer or join story time
questions.hint: Libraries have many fun activities for kids!

questions.question: Why is a library called a 'public' place?
options: Because anyone in the community can use it for free
questions.hint: Public means open to all people, and it costs nothing to visit.

questions.question: How does a library card work?
options: You sign up, borrow books, and return them on time
You buy the card and keep the books
You use it to open doors
questions.hint: The card lets you borrow and return items.

questions.question: What happens when everyone takes care of library books?
options: More people can enjoy them for a long time
questions.hint: Shared things last longer when people are careful.

questions.question: What services does a modern library offer besides books?
options: Computer access, programs, and meeting rooms
questions.hint: Libraries have grown to offer many community resources.

questions.question: Who delivers letters and packages to your home?
questions.hint: They carry a big bag and walk from house to house.

questions.question: Where does a mail carrier bring your letters?
questions.hint: A small box near your front door.

questions.question: What do you put on a letter so it gets to the right place?
questions.hint: It tells the mail carrier which house the letter goes to.

questions.question: What is a post office?
options: A place where mail is sorted and sent
A place where food is made
questions.hint: You can buy stamps and send packages here.

questions.question: Why is mail delivery an important service?
options: It connects people and businesses across the community
questions.hint: People depend on mail for letters, bills, and packages.

questions.question: In Canada, which organisation delivers most of the mail?
questions.hint: Their trucks and mailboxes are red.

questions.question: Why does every house have a unique address?
options: So mail and emergency services can find it
To make the house look fancy
questions.hint: Your address is like your home's special name.

questions.question: What is a postal code?
options: A set of letters and numbers that identifies your area
A secret password for the post office
questions.hint: In Canada it looks like A1A 1A1 — letters and numbers mixed together.

questions.question: Who fixes cars when they break down?
questions.hint: They use tools like wrenches and work in a garage.

questions.question: Where does a mechanic work?
questions.hint: You bring your car here when it needs fixing.

questions.question: What tool does a mechanic use to tighten bolts?
questions.hint: It turns and grips metal pieces.

questions.question: Why do cars need to visit a mechanic?
options: To stay safe and working properly
questions.hint: Mechanics check things like brakes and tires to keep us safe.

questions.question: Why is it important to change the oil in a car?
options: It keeps the engine running smoothly
It makes the car look shiny
It makes the car go faster
questions.hint: Oil helps the engine parts move without getting too hot.

questions.question: What should you check on a car before a long road trip?
questions.hint: These things help keep everyone safe on the road.

questions.question: What does a tow truck do?
options: It carries broken cars to the auto shop
questions.hint: When a car can't drive anymore, this truck comes to help.

questions.question: Why do tires need to have enough air?
options: So the car drives safely and uses less gas
So the car makes more noise
questions.hint: Flat tires can make driving dangerous.

questions.question: Who helps keep our community safe from danger?
questions.hint: They wear a badge and sometimes drive a car with flashing lights.

questions.question: What vehicle do police officers drive?
questions.hint: It often has flashing red and blue lights.

questions.question: If you are lost, who is a safe person to ask for help?
questions.hint: They are trained to help people who need it.

questions.question: What is one rule police officers help everyone follow?
options: Run as fast as you can
questions.hint: Red means stop, green means go!

questions.question: Why do communities have rules and laws?
options: To keep everyone safe and fair
To give police something to do
questions.hint: Rules help people live together peacefully.

questions.question: What should you do if you see someone being bullied?
questions.hint: Adults can help stop bullying and keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What does a crosswalk help people do safely?
questions.hint: The white lines on the road tell drivers to stop for walkers.

questions.question: Who is responsible for following community rules?
questions.hint: Rules work best when everybody follows them.

questions.question: Who helps you learn to read and count at school?
questions.hint: They stand at the front of your classroom.

questions.question: Where do teachers work?
questions.hint: A building with classrooms, a playground, and a bell.

questions.question: Why is it important to be kind to classmates?
options: So everyone feels happy and safe
So you can be the boss
questions.hint: A friendly classroom is a better place to learn.

questions.question: What is one rule you follow at school?
questions.hint: This lets everyone take turns talking.

questions.question: How does a school help a community?
options: It gives children a place to learn and grow
questions.hint: Education is one of the most important services a community provides.

questions.question: What responsibility do students have at school?
options: To try their best and respect others
questions.hint: Being a good student means working hard and being respectful.

questions.question: Why do schools have rules about safety?
options: To protect everyone from getting hurt
To keep it quiet for the principal
questions.hint: Fire drills, no running in halls — these all keep people safe.

questions.question: How do families and schools work together?
options: Parents and teachers talk about how to help children learn
Families teach math at home only
Schools tell parents what to do
questions.hint: Parent-teacher nights and school events bring families and schools together.

questions.question: Who takes care of sick animals?
questions.hint: They are like doctors, but for animals!

questions.question: Where do you take your pet when it is sick?
questions.hint: This is a special place where animals get help.

questions.question: What does a vet use to listen to an animal's heart?
questions.hint: Doctors use this too — it has two earpieces and a round end.

questions.question: Which of these animals might visit a vet?
questions.hint: Vets help pets and other animals stay healthy.

questions.question: Why do pets need to get vaccines?
options: To protect them from getting sick
questions.hint: Vaccines help the body fight off diseases before they start.

questions.question: What is one responsibility of having a pet?
options: Making sure it has food, water, and visits the vet
Letting it do whatever it wants
Only playing with it on weekends
questions.hint: Pets depend on their owners to take care of them.

questions.question: What does it mean to spay or neuter a pet?
options: A small operation so the pet cannot have babies
Buying the pet a new collar
questions.hint: This helps control the number of animals that need homes.

questions.question: Why should you not feed chocolate to a dog?
options: It can make dogs very sick
questions.hint: Some foods that are fine for people are dangerous for animals.

questions.question: What is the main public transit system in Toronto called?
questions.hint: It runs buses, streetcars, and subways.

questions.question: Why might a community in Northern Ontario rely more on cars than buses?
options: Towns are spread far apart with fewer bus routes
People in the north prefer walking
Northern roads are too wide for buses
questions.hint: Long distances between communities make bus routes impractical.

questions.question: What information does a transit map show?
options: Bus and train routes, stops, and connections
questions.hint: It helps riders plan their journey from one place to another.

questions.question: How does transportation infrastructure connect Ontario communities?
options: Highways, railways, and airports link cities and towns
questions.hint: Highway 401, Via Rail, and airports help people and goods move across the province.

questions.question: Which region of Ontario is known for growing many fruits like peaches and grapes?
questions.hint: This area is near a famous waterfall.

questions.question: Why might a town near the ocean have more seafood restaurants?
options: People near the ocean don't like meat
There are no farms near oceans
questions.hint: Local food often depends on what is available close by.

questions.question: What is a 'food bank' and why do communities need them?
options: A place that gives free food to families who need it
A bank that loans money for food
questions.hint: Some families need help getting enough food.

questions.question: What does 'locally grown' mean on a menu?
options: The food was grown nearby, not far away
The food grew inside the restaurant
The food is from another country
questions.hint: Local means close to where you live.

questions.question: Why do communities create 'zoning' rules for where buildings can go?
options: To keep homes, shops, and factories in the right areas
questions.hint: You wouldn't want a noisy factory next to a school.

questions.question: What does a street name sign help people do?
options: Find their way around the community
Learn the name of the mayor
questions.hint: Every road has a name so people can give and follow directions.

questions.question: How has transportation infrastructure in Ontario changed since the 1800s?
options: From canals and dirt roads to highways and railways
Cars were always the main way to travel
questions.hint: Early settlers used waterways; now we have Highway 401.

questions.question: Why must builders follow building codes?
options: To make sure buildings are safe for people
questions.hint: Codes are rules about how strong and safe a building must be.

questions.question: In rural parts of Ontario, why might people travel far to see a doctor?
options: There are fewer hospitals in rural areas
questions.hint: Smaller communities sometimes don't have their own hospital.

questions.question: What does OHIP provide for people in Ontario?
questions.hint: It's a card that helps pay for doctor visits.

questions.question: On a community map, a hospital is usually shown with which symbol?
questions.hint: Look for the letter that starts the word 'Hospital'.

questions.question: Why do ambulances need clear roads to travel fast?
options: To reach patients quickly in emergencies
questions.hint: Every second counts when someone is very sick or hurt.

questions.question: Which part of Ontario has the most farmland?
questions.hint: The flat land and warmer weather in the south are better for crops.

questions.question: What is one reason Indigenous peoples in Ontario farmed the Three Sisters (corn, beans, squash)?
options: The three plants help each other grow
They were the only plants available
They could not find other food
questions.hint: Corn grows tall, beans climb it, and squash covers the ground.

questions.question: On a land-use map, what colour usually shows farmland?
questions.hint: Think about the colour of fields and crops.

questions.question: What challenge do Ontario farmers face due to urban sprawl?
options: Farmland is being turned into housing
Too many people want to be farmers
questions.hint: Cities and suburbs keep growing outward onto land that was once farmed.

questions.question: In Ontario, who is responsible for making fire safety rules for buildings?
options: The local fire department and government
questions.hint: Fire codes are created by community leaders to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What is the 'Stop, Drop, and Roll' rule for?
questions.hint: Rolling on the ground smothers flames.

questions.question: How do fire hydrants help firefighters?
options: They provide a water supply on the street
questions.hint: Firefighters connect hoses to these red or yellow objects on sidewalks.

questions.question: Why do firefighters inspect buildings in the community?
options: To check that fire safety rules are followed
questions.hint: They make sure exits, alarms, and sprinklers are working.

questions.question: How do public libraries help people who are new to Canada?
options: They offer language classes, settlement info, and free resources
questions.hint: Libraries are often one of the first places newcomers visit for help.

questions.question: On a community map, which symbol might show a library?
questions.hint: The symbol relates to what you do there — read!

questions.question: Why might a small community and a big city have different-sized libraries?
options: Bigger populations need bigger libraries with more resources
Cities have more money to waste
questions.hint: More people means more demand for books and programs.

questions.question: How did people share stories in communities before public libraries existed?
options: Through oral storytelling passed down through generations
questions.hint: Indigenous and early communities used spoken words to share knowledge.

questions.question: How do postal codes help sort mail across Canada?
options: The first letter tells which province or region the mail goes to
They tell how heavy the package is
They show the colour of the mailbox
questions.hint: K is for eastern Ontario, M is for Toronto, and so on.

questions.question: How did communities in early Canada communicate before a postal system?
options: By sending messengers on foot, horse, or canoe
They could not communicate at all
questions.hint: Travel was slow, so messages took days or weeks.

questions.question: Why might mail delivery be harder in northern Ontario communities?
options: Long distances and rough terrain make travel difficult
The mail carrier doesn't like snow
There are no addresses in the north
questions.hint: Some communities are very far from cities and hard to reach.

questions.question: How has communication changed from letters to today?
options: People now also use email, texts, and video calls
Letters are still the only way
questions.hint: Technology has given us many new ways to stay in touch.

questions.question: Why are auto shops important in rural Ontario communities?
options: People depend on cars because towns are far apart
Cars are only used in cities
questions.hint: In areas with less public transit, cars are the main way to get around.

questions.question: What happens at a vehicle safety inspection in Ontario?
options: A mechanic checks that the car meets safety standards
The car gets a new paint job
The driver takes a written test
The car is washed and waxed
questions.hint: The government requires this to make sure cars on the road are safe.

questions.question: How have cars changed communities over time?
options: People can live farther from where they work and shop
People stopped travelling after cars were invented
Cars are only used for fun
questions.hint: Cars let people travel longer distances every day.

questions.question: Why might a community need more than one auto shop?
options: More people and cars means more repairs are needed
Auto shops are only for decoration
questions.hint: As a community grows, so does the need for services.

questions.question: In Canada, who makes the laws that communities must follow?
questions.hint: People vote for leaders who create and change laws.

questions.question: What is the difference between a rule and a law?
options: Laws are official and enforced by government; rules can be informal
questions.hint: Laws are written down by government and apply to everyone.

questions.question: Why do different communities sometimes have different by-laws?
questions.hint: A fishing village and a big city need different rules.

questions.question: On a map, a police station might be marked with which symbol?
questions.hint: Think about what a police officer wears on their chest.

questions.question: In Ontario, who is responsible for making sure all children can go to school?
questions.hint: The Ontario government creates education laws and funds schools.

questions.question: Why do some Ontario communities have both public and Catholic school boards?
options: The Canadian Constitution protects both systems
There are too many students for one system
questions.hint: This right is written into Canada's founding document.

questions.question: How did schools in early Ontario communities differ from schools today?
options: They were one-room schoolhouses with all ages together
questions.hint: Long ago, one teacher taught children of all ages in a single room.

questions.question: Why is it important that schools teach about different cultures?
options: So students understand and respect the diverse community they live in
Because the law says you must speak many languages
questions.hint: Canada is home to people from many different backgrounds.

questions.question: How do vets in rural Ontario differ from city vets?
options: They often treat farm animals like cows and horses too
questions.hint: Farms have large animals that also need medical care.

questions.question: What is an animal shelter?
options: A place where lost or homeless animals are cared for until they find a family
questions.hint: Shelters give animals a safe place to stay and help them get adopted.

questions.question: Why might a community need a bylaw about pets?
options: To keep both people and animals safe
To make sure all pets are the same colour
questions.hint: Rules like leash laws and licensing help the community run smoothly.

questions.question: How do veterinarians help Ontario's farming communities?
options: They keep livestock healthy so farms can produce food
They only help pets in cities
questions.hint: Healthy animals are important for the food we eat.
